Names: Left Rostrolateral Prefrontal Cortex (Lateral subdivision BA10 lateral)
Comment: ROI internal. Core UC for relational integration in deductive reasoning. Integrates multiple relations to derive logical conclusions. Belongs to executive control network. Corresponds to lateral BA10.
Output Semantics: [RLPFC-Lateral] Integrated inference result. Logical conclusion (A>C) derived by integrating multiple relations (A>B B>C) with general rules (transitivity). Includes validity and confidence of the conclusion. Result of relational integration computation representing the consequence of rules applied to specific problems.
Requirement: To realize Deductive Reasoning [U.RLPFC-Lateral] integrates multiple individual relations (input: contextualized relational representations provided by [U.RLPFC-Medial] with Output Semantics of contextualized relational representation) and general logical rules (input: spatial structure representation from [U.PPC-SPL] with Output Semantics of spatial rule structure and formal structure from [U.PPC-IPL] with Output Semantics of logical argument structure) to derive logically valid conclusions (output: [U.RLPFC-Lateral] integrated inference result with Output Semantics of integrated inference). This process references and updates working memory (input/output: [U.DLPFC] with Output Semantics of working memory contents) and verifies reasoning validity through error monitoring signals (input/output: [U.dACC] with Output Semantics of error/conflict detection). Final inference results are sent to action selection (output: [U.PMC]) emotional evaluation (output: [U.rACC]) and rule representation updates (output: [U.PPC-SPL] [U.PPC-IPL]).
Requirement realization by interface: [U.RLPFC-Medial] provides contextualized relations (e.g. episodically structured premises such as 'A is larger than B' and 'B is larger than C'). These are integrated with logical rule structures provided by [U.PPC-SPL] and [U.PPC-IPL] (transitivity rule: 'If X>Y and Y>Z then X>Z'). While referencing intermediate results held in [U.DLPFC] working memory buffer relational integration computation is executed to derive logical conclusion ('A is larger than C'). Error signals from [U.dACC] verify reasoning consistency and evaluate confidence. Integrated inference result is written back to [U.DLPFC] sent to [U.dACC] as monitoring information to [U.rACC] for emotional evaluation and to [U.PMC] for action selection. Rule application results are fed back to [U.PPC-SPL] and [U.PPC-IPL] updating rule representations. Bidirectional connection with [U.MDT] adjusts cognitive control state. Thus the relational integration function required by Requirement is realized through input/output defined in Interface.
Capability: Receives multiple relational representations (relation 1 relation 2 ...) and abstract rule (rule) integrates them to generate new relational conclusion (integrated relation). This Capability operates based solely on structural properties of relations independent of semantic content ('larger' 'faster' etc.) of input relations. Applicable to relational integration tasks in arbitrary domains. This computation dynamically binds multiple distributed representations constructing new relations in hierarchical representation space. Neuroscientific basis: Wendelken et al. (2008) demonstrated RLPFC specializes in relational integration not relational encoding. Christoff et al. (2001) showed RLPFC plays core role in relational integration. Computational basis: Halford et al. (1998) relational complexity theory showed relational integration is essence of cognitive complexity. Duncan et al. (2020) revealed relational integration is supported by dynamic network mechanisms accompanied by increased phase synchrony and functional connectivity in frontoparietal network.
Mechanism: Relational integration is realized through dynamic binding mechanism in frontoparietal network. Specifically (1) individual relational representations from hippocampus (received from [U.RLPFC-Medial]) (2) rule structures from parietal cortex (received from [U.PPC-SPL] [U.PPC-IPL]) and (3) working memory space ([U.DLPFC]) are dynamically bound. This binding process is characterized by increased phase synchrony and strengthened functional connectivity. RLPFC functions as top-down effective connectivity source in this dynamic network dynamically binding rules coded throughout working memory systems. Bound representations are constructed as new relations in hierarchical representation space. Error monitoring ([U.dACC]) verifies binding consistency triggering recalculation when inconsistencies are detected. Integration process is stabilized by decreased network metastability and confidence is evaluated. Final integrated result is sent in parallel to multiple downstream systems ([U.DLPFC] [U.dACC] [U.rACC] [U.PMC] [U.PPC-SPL] [U.PPC-IPL]).
Implementation: [U.RLPFC-Lateral] = Integrate([U.RLPFC-Medial], [U.PPC-SPL], [U.PPC-IPL], [U.DLPFC]_read) ∧ Verify([U.dACC]); [U.DLPFC]_write = [U.RLPFC-Lateral]; [U.dACC]_monitor = Validity([U.RLPFC-Lateral]); [U.rACC] = Evaluate([U.RLPFC-Lateral]); [U.PMC] = SelectAction([U.RLPFC-Lateral]); [U.PPC-SPL] = UpdateRule_spatial([U.RLPFC-Lateral]); [U.PPC-IPL] = UpdateRule_structural([U.RLPFC-Lateral]); [U.MDT] = Feedback([U.RLPFC-Lateral])

Names: Left Rostrolateral Prefrontal Cortex (Medial subdivision BA10 medial)
Comment: ROI internal. Handles integration of episodic memory information and self-related processing. Belongs to default mode network. Corresponds to medial BA10. Maintains contextual information in deductive reasoning.
Output Semantics: [RLPFC-Medial] Contextualized relational representation. Episodically structured relational representation integrating individual relation information from hippocampus with task context. Contextual bundle of premises needed for reasoning.
Requirement: To structure premises in Deductive Reasoning [U.RLPFC-Medial] integrates individual relational information from hippocampus (input: [U.HPC] individual relational encoding with Output Semantics of individual relational encoding) with task context information (input: [U.mPFC] task context and goal state with Output Semantics of task context and goal) to generate episodically structured relational representation (output: [U.RLPFC-Medial] contextualized relational representation with Output Semantics of contextualized relational representation). This integrated representation is sent to [U.RLPFC-Lateral] as reasoning material for relational integration computation. Bidirectional connection with thalamus (input/output: [U.MDT] with Output Semantics of integrated cognitive control signal) supports information integration in default mode network.
Requirement realization by interface: Receives individual relational information from [U.HPC] (e.g. individual episodes such as 'A beat B in trial 1' and 'B beat C in trial 2') and task context from [U.mPFC] ('task to infer transitive relations' as goal state and evaluation criteria). Integrates these to generate episodically structured relational representation (contextualized premises such as 'A is stronger than B' and 'B is stronger than C'). Bidirectional connection with [U.MDT] supports self-related processing and memory integration in default mode network. Structured relational representation is sent to [U.RLPFC-Lateral] as material for relational integration computation. Integration state is fed back to [U.MDT]. Thus the contextual integration function required by Requirement is realized through input/output defined in Interface.
Capability: Receives individual episodic representations (episodic representation 1 episodic representation 2 ...) and task demand (task demand) integrates them to generate contextually structured relational representation (contextualized relational representation). This Capability functions as general process of extracting relational structure and contextual integration independent of specific content of episodic memory ('won' 'larger' etc.). Applicable to structuring relational episodic information in arbitrary domains. Neuroscientific basis: Bludau et al. (2014) connectivity-based parcellation identified medial BA10 as independent cluster from lateral belonging to default mode network. Catani et al. (2023) showed medial BA10 is directly connected to hippocampus as part of memory stream. Computational basis: Relational extraction from episodic memory is process of constructing abstract relations through integration of individual events. Default mode network specializes in integration of internally generated representations (Buckner et al. 2008).
Mechanism: Episodic memory integration is realized through information transformation in hippocampal-PFC circuit. Specifically (1) individual episodes from hippocampal CA1/subiculum (received from [U.HPC]) are (2) selectively activated by task context from medial PFC (received from [U.mPFC]) and (3) contextually reconstructed in default mode network. In this reconstruction process individual episodes are abstracted from temporal/spatial context and relational structure is extracted. For example abstract relation 'A is stronger than B' is extracted from episode 'A beat B in trial 1'. By integrating multiple episodes consistent relational representation (transitive structure 'A>B>C') is constructed. Bidirectional connection with MD thalamus ([U.MDT]) coordinates this integration process with global cognitive control state. Constructed contextualized representation is sent to [U.RLPFC-Lateral] as input to executive control network for further integration computation.
